title: COREDB: add isolated test-world make targets and CI wiring
description: Wire day-to-day and CI workflows to isolated DB profiles so safe behavior is the default.\n\nGoal: developers and automation use explicit test-world targets instead of writing to canonical DB.
design: Scope is Makefile/scripts/.github workflow wiring and env profile propagation only. Keep target names simple and stable.
acceptance_criteria:
Add make targets for isolated execution (for example: test-isolated, smoke-isolated, test-world-reset).

Targets export explicit test profile/env and call existing command surface; default test/smoke entry points no longer encourage canonical DB writes.

CI workflow uses isolated profile for workspace tests/smoke-related checks where applicable.

Do NOT: rework command output formats; introduce new product specs; add evidence storage.

Verification: run each new make target locally; inspect CI config diff to confirm isolated env is set; run one intentional non-isolated smoke invocation and confirm guard blocks it.

Close: common local/CI paths for tests and smoke are isolated-by-default.
close_reason: Added Makefile targets test-isolated, smoke/smoke-isolated, test-world-reset with scripts/with-isolated-test-profile + scripts/test-world-reset; delegated make test via test-isolated; scripts/run and CI export COHERENCE_DB_PROFILE=test and run make test-isolated.

title: COREDB: enforce isolated test world guardrails (ADR-0004)
description: Implement hard safety boundaries so smoke/tests cannot mutate canonical repository DB by accident.\n\nGoal: test and smoke workflows fail fast unless an explicit isolated test-world profile is active.
design: Boundary: this task adds guardrails and profile plumbing only; no evidence-store model and no broad CLI UX redesign.
acceptance_criteria:
Add explicit runtime guard (shared helper) used by m0-smoke and m1-spec-smoke that requires an isolated profile (for example COHERENCE_DB_PROFILE=test) before any write path runs.

Guard error is explicit and actionable, and refuses canonical/default profile with guidance on env/target to use.

Apply same policy to Rust test DB helpers (maybe_conn-style helpers in store/link/verify tests): tests that would write without isolated profile are skipped or fail with a clear message (pick one behavior and keep it consistent).

Do NOT: implement managed evidence snapshots; add new schema tables; change verify-ac/verify-spec semantics.

Verification: run smoke command once without test profile (must fail); run with test profile (must pass); run cargo test --workspace under isolated profile (must pass); confirm canonical DB no longer receives new smoke fixture rows from default invocation.

Close: no smoke/test write path mutates canonical DB unless explicitly configured as test world.
close_reason: Added test_world_guard: COHERENCE_DB_PROFILE=test required before smoke writes or test maybe_conn migrations; wired m0-smoke/m1-spec-smoke; integration tests panic with guidance if unset; scripts/run CI Makefile propagate isolated profile.

title: COREDB-16 — Add minimal Spec/AC command surface
description:
Thin CLI wrapper over existing spec repository functions (COREDB-8). No new persistence model.

Goal: humans and later tools can create and inspect Spec/AC records without hardcoded smoke data. Sits after COREDB-9 (smoke proof), before COREDB-10 (codeintel schema).
design: Boundary: persistence stays in COREDB-8 functions; this task is command surface only.
acceptance_criteria:
Commands (names may match CLI style): `spec add`, `spec list`, `spec show <SPEC_ID>`, `ac add --spec-id <SPEC_ID>`, `ac list --spec-id <SPEC_ID>`.

spec add: support at least --id (optional/generated), --slug, --title, --description, --level, --status.

ac add: support at least --id (optional/generated), --spec-id, --title, --intent, --review-mode, --risk-level, --concern (repeatable if easy).

Use existing spec_store / repository functions; assume schema via migrate; print created IDs clearly; stable output for copy-paste into later codeintel tasks.

Example flow: `cargo run -p coherence-core-db -- spec add --slug coredb-spec-store --title "core-db persists specs" --description "Spec records stored and read through Dolt" --level module --status draft` then `ac add` with linked spec-id.

Do NOT: codeintel; test links; verification runner; separate coherence-spec-cli; final UX; docs export; SQLx/TinyORM; ad-hoc SQL in handlers (use repository layer).

Verification: `make tool run`; live commands create Spec and AC; spec list / ac list show them; `m1-spec-smoke` still passes.

Close: manual Spec and AC creation works; IDs can be copied into codeintel-linking tasks.
close_reason: Added spec/ac CLI subcommands (add, list, show / add, list) wired to spec_store with argv parsing, migrations before DB ops, stable tab/key-value output and generated SPEC-GEN/AC-GEN IDs; verified make tool run and m1-spec-smoke.

title: COREDB-13 — Add spec verification report
description:
Spec-level aggregation over COREDB-12 runner and link storage.

Goal: given Spec id, list ACs, run/collect linked verification per AC, print spec health report; nonzero exit if any linked verification fails.
design: Review smell: if COREDB-13 adds evidence/artifact tables, stop — later M1/M2.
acceptance_criteria:
Command e.g. `verify-spec <SPEC_ID>`. Load ACs for spec; for each AC list links; use COREDB-12 logic; statuses passed/failed/skipped/no_verification. Summary counts: specs 1, acceptance_criteria N, passed/failed/skipped/no_verification. Stable output for evidence.

Do NOT: full review/evidence system; docs export; Temporal; coverage; SCIP graph; codeintel schema changes unless tiny missing field blocks report.

Verification: `make tool run`; live flow Spec+AC+CodeLocation+link => verify-spec passed summary; failing command => nonzero; no-link AC clear.

Close: one Spec produces meaningful AC verification report from linked commands.
close_reason: Implemented coherence-core-db verify-spec: COREDB-12 aggregation per AC, SPEC summary row with counts (specs=1), tab-stable AC/LINK/SUMMARY lines, nonzero exit on command failure; AcVerifyOverallStatus + skipped rollup for ACs with only skipped links.

title: COREDB-7 — Add spec module relational schema
description: Evaluate and wire migration execution library for core-db M1 using refinery against Dolt SQL while keeping module-owned schema layout.
acceptance_criteria: refinery wired for migration execution; module migration layout under sql/modules/spec/migrations; versioned migration applies specs/acceptance_criteria/acceptance_criterion_concerns/spec_relations; live migrate succeeds against Dolt; m0-smoke remains green via migration path; decision note captures buy-vs-build and ownership split.
close_reason: Reshaped spec schema to module migration layout under sql/modules/spec/migrations and switched m0-smoke to this source while preserving live M0 behavior.

title: COREDB-8 — Implement spec store put/list/read functions
description: Implement persistence functions for M1 spec module.
acceptance_criteria: put_spec/get_spec/list_specs/put_acceptance_criterion/list_acceptance_criteria_for_spec/put_spec_relation/list_spec_relations_for_spec exist; concerns persist and read back; SQL parameters used; no SQLx/TinyORM adoption in this task; use existing mysql crate path and refinery-applied schema.
close_reason: Implemented manual mysql repository mapping for spec domain with focused round-trip tests (spec, AC concerns, relations) on refinery-managed schema, with no CLI evidence runner and no legacy fallback path.

title: COREDB-10 — Add minimal codeintel schema for code locations and AC links
description:
Schema/migration only for codeintel module. No repository functions yet.

Goal: smallest codeintel-owned schema to link ACs to test files or test commands. Module layout under sql/modules/codeintel/migrations/.
design: Review smell: if COREDB-10 adds put_code_location or link commands, stop — that is COREDB-11.
acceptance_criteria:
Migration creates `codeintel_code_locations` and `codeintel_ac_links`.

codeintel_code_locations: id, repo_path, file_path, kind, symbol nullable, test_command nullable, created_at, updated_at.

codeintel_ac_links: id, ac_id, code_location_id, relation_kind, note, created_at, updated_at.

relation_kind supports at least: verified_by, implemented_by, touched_by.

Comments in SQL: module codeintel; owner codeintel module; applied_by coherence-core-db migration path. FKs optional for M1 — decision explicit in migration comments.

Wire into refinery/embed same pattern as spec module (core-db owns execution).

Do NOT: repository functions; CLI; test runner; SCIP/symbol graph; codeintel-cli; verify-spec; test_run storage unless scoped.

Verification: `make tool run`; live migrate on Dolt; show sql/modules tree; `m1-spec-smoke` still passes; spec/ac CLI from COREDB-16 still works.

Close: tables exist via migration; spec module ownership unchanged.
close_reason: Added codeintel module migration (codeintel_code_locations, codeintel_ac_links) under sql/modules/codeintel/migrations; embedded second refinery runner with refinery_schema_history_codeintel to avoid V1 collision with spec module; apply_all runs spec then codeintel. Verified: make tool run, m1-spec-smoke, Dolt tables present, spec list.

title: COREDB-11 — Implement AC to test link storage
description:
Repository/storage only for codeintel links. Minimal Rust models if needed.

Goal: persist and read links from AcceptanceCriteria to code/test locations. COREDB-12 must consume readback without raw SQL.
design: Review smell: if COREDB-11 executes shell commands, stop — that is COREDB-12.
acceptance_criteria:
Models: CodeLocation, CodeLocationKind, AcCodeLink, AcCodeRelationKind (as needed).

Functions: put_code_location; get_code_location if useful; put_ac_code_link; list_code_links_for_ac.

Support: AC verified_by test file; verified_by test command; optional symbol. SQL parameterized; no DDL in repos; schema from migrate; repeated links per AC allowed; return enough data for COREDB-12 to run test commands.

Do NOT: execute test commands; verify-spec; full evidence/SCIP; codeintel-cli; SQLx/TinyORM.

Verification: `make tool run`; focused Rust tests for put/list location, put/list AC link, verified_by round-trip; optional live smoke: Spec + AC + CodeLocation(test_command) + AcCodeLink.

Close: AC linkable to test command/file and read back via repository.
close_reason: Implemented codeintel_repo: CodeLocation/CodeLocationKind, AcCodeLink/AcCodeRelationKind, AcCodeLinkWithLocation; put/get CodeLocation, put/list AcCodeLink with locations; parameterized SQL; tests for round-trip and verified_by with spec+AC.

title: COREDB-12 — Add minimal linked test runner
description:
Run linked test commands for one AC. No spec-level report (COREDB-13).

Goal: given AC id, find verified_by links, run linked commands, report passed/failed/skipped. Expose a reusable internal result type for COREDB-13 (not only stdout).
design: Review smell: if COREDB-12 aggregates whole Spec status, stop — that is COREDB-13. Provide structured results, not only println.
acceptance_criteria:
Command or function e.g. `verify-ac <AC_ID>`. Load links via COREDB-11. Only run relation_kind verified_by with kind command or test_file where test_command present.

Behavior: no links => skipped/no_verification; exit 0 => passed; nonzero => failed; missing command => skipped with reason. Per-link output: AC id, code_location id, command, status, short output summary. Result type reusable by COREDB-13.

Optional: minimal run persistence if cheap; else in-memory/report only.

Do NOT: spec-level report; artifacts/traces; Temporal; workflow runner; sandbox model; non-verified relation kinds execution.

Verification: `make tool run`; passing linked command => passed; failing command => failed nonzero; no-link => clear skipped.

Close: one AC verifiable by linked test command(s).
close_reason: Added verify-ac CLI and ac_verify module: loads verified_by links via list_code_links_for_ac, runs test_command with sh -c, structured AcVerifyAcRunResult for COREDB-13; tests + integration cli_smoke under crate tests/

title: COREDB-9 — Add M1 spec smoke command
description:
Smoke command only. Prove the M1 spec store works end-to-end against live Dolt.

Goal: add a command that proves Spec / AcceptanceCriterion / SpecRelation persistence works through the current repository/store layer and refinery-applied schema.
design: Review smell: if COREDB-9 adds generic `spec add`, stop — that belongs in COREDB-16.
acceptance_criteria:
Deliverable: add command `m1-spec-smoke` (name may match existing CLI style). Command connects to live Dolt using existing connection policy; applies migrations through existing migration path; creates one Spec, one AcceptanceCriterion for that Spec, one SpecRelation if repository supports it; reads everything back via repository functions; prints stable summary.

Output includes: connection_mode; migration status or migrate success signal; spec count; AC count; relation count; final line `m1-spec-smoke: success`.

Do NOT: codeintel tables; AC-to-test links; verify-spec; generic graph model; polished spec/ac CLI UX (that is COREDB-16); new store functions beyond COREDB-8; SQLx/TinyORM.

Verification: `make tool run`; `cargo run -p coherence-core-db -- m1-spec-smoke`; `m0-smoke` still passes if present; show diff summary and final command output.

Close: live Dolt run proves migrate + put/read/list for Spec/AC/SpecRelation.
close_reason: Added m1-spec-smoke CLI: refinery migrations, Dolt connection, spec_store put/get/list for Spec AC and self SpecRelation; prints connection_mode migrations_applied spec_count ac_count relation_count and success line. Verified make tool run, m0-smoke and m1-spec-smoke against live Dolt.

title: COREDB: bootstrap managed per-run evidence store skeleton (ADR-0005)
description: Introduce minimal runtime evidence scaffolding separate from canonical DB, aligned with ADR-0005.\n\nGoal: define where per-run evidence lives and persist pointer metadata without coupling to runtime DB backend.
design: M0 skeleton only: file-based per-run layout plus typed metadata contract. Keep backend simple (JSON/files), no heavy adapter framework yet.
acceptance_criteria:
Define minimal run evidence layout under .coherence/runs/<run-id>/ with metadata and artifact pointer locations.

Add typed envelope/metadata model for observation records (run_id, plan_id optional, ac_id optional, observation_id, object_kind, object_id, payload summary/hash, redaction policy id optional).

Ensure canonical DB path stores only pointers/metadata references (or explicit TODO boundary if schema for pointers is deferred), never heavy payload blobs.

Do NOT: require app runtime to use Dolt; implement full adapter SDK; store all snapshots inline in canonical tables.

Verification: create one sample run record end-to-end (metadata + artifact pointer); show retrieval path from canonical metadata to run evidence location; confirm large payload stays outside canonical DB.

Close: evidence-store direction is executable and separated from canonical reasoning state.

title: COREDB: canonical DB protection policy and docs update
description: Document and enforce the operational policy that canonical repository DB contains curated reasoning state only.\n\nGoal: policy is visible in CLI/help/docs and failures provide clear remediation.
design: Policy surface only: messaging, guard text, and docs alignment with ADR-0004. No schema changes.
acceptance_criteria:
Update AGENTS and/or command help text to reflect rule: tests never write canonical DB and require isolated profile.

Standardize refusal message for blocked writes so users know exactly which env/target to run next.

Add one short operator-oriented section describing test world lifecycle (create, migrate, run, destroy, optional keep-on-fail).

Do NOT: implement new migration tables; redesign CLI command taxonomy.

Verification: run help/context docs commands and confirm policy text is present; trigger refusal path and validate message clarity and consistency.

Close: policy is explicit, discoverable, and consistent across docs/help/error paths.

title: COREDB-14 — Document M1 module ownership boundaries
description:
Documentation only for M1 module ownership (tiny wording fixes in code allowed if needed).

Goal: one place explains physical co-location vs logical owners, current M1 command flow, and explicit non-goals.
design: Do after COREDB-13 so docs match reality, not fantasy.
acceptance_criteria:
Cover: one repo-local Dolt DB, multiple logical modules; core-db owns lifecycle + migration execution; migration mechanics via library; spec vs codeintel table ownership; beads/deliverables/workflow out of this M1 slice; boundaries visible in layout/comments.

Document M1 flow: migrate; spec add; ac add; code location/link; verify-ac; verify-spec (names as implemented).

Explicit non-goals: full SCIP; docs export; Temporal; artifact store; generic graph; final spec-cli UX.

Do NOT: schema/repo/command changes except docs (or trivial wording); new tasks unless doc gap requires follow-up.

Verification: `make tool run`; doc names match implemented commands; ownership explicit.

Close: new reader understands who owns which tables and what M1 proves.
close_reason: Document M1 boundaries in AGENTS.md (one DB, spec vs codeintel tables, migrate/refinery orchestration, CLI flow migrate/spec add/ac add/codeintel_repo/verify-ac/verify-spec, explicit non-goals); cross-linked module comments in main, migrations, spec_store, ac_code_link_store, ac_verify. Verified: make tool run.

acceptance_criteria: Document DOLT_SOCKET/DOLT_HOST/DOLT_PORT/DOLT_DB config; document socket-preferred/TCP-fallback policy; document m0-smoke run steps; avoid claiming full integration.

title: COREDB-15 — Evaluate TinyORM/SQLx for CRUD repository boilerplate
description:
Spike / decision note only. Not mainline M1. Do not adopt SQLx/TinyORM in production.

Goal: compare mysql+refinery manual repos vs SQLx vs TinyORM; Dolt compatibility; boilerplate estimate; migration impact; explicit recommendation.
design: Not M1 critical path. Prefer depending on COREDB-14 so eval runs after M1 slice is documented. P3.
acceptance_criteria:
Deliverable: short decision note (e.g. docs/decisions/ or .coherence/stubs); optional isolated spike; recommendation: stay manual / adopt SQLx later / TinyORM / defer.

Do NOT: rewrite DB layer; switch COREDB repos to SQLx; change migrations/commands; block COREDB-9..14.

Verification: `make tool run`; spike isolated if present; recommendation explicit.

Close: clear whether to revisit ORM/SQLx and what future task would adopt it.
close_reason: Delivered decision note at .coherence/stubs/coredb-15-sqlx-tinyorm-repository-decision.txt: stay manual mysql+SQL for M1; defer SQLx pilot until schema/async needs justify it; defer TinyORM (SQLx stack + MSRV>workspace). make tool run passed. Revisit via future pilot task for one module.
